what: THE GUARD THAT ENFORCES 'THE MANAGER MAY NOT TAKE AN ITEM' IS NOW STRUCTURALLY BLIND, AND IT FAILS OPEN. scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py derives WHO THE MANAGER IS from the git history of docs/claude/work/MANAGER-LEASE.json -- deliberately, and its docstring argues at length why branch-name and register-authorship were both rejected as identifiers. The 2026-09-21 reset ARCHIVED that lease file. Measured 2026-09-21 on branch claude/metis-insights-manager-9qmm63 with four manager commits in the range: the guard returned 'manager-scope: no_manager_commits ... 0 manager commit(s) in 4 commit(s) graded', exit 0. [!] THE EXIT CODE IS THE PROBLEM. A guard that cannot identify its subject reports GREEN, so 'no violation' and 'could not look' are collapsed into one value -- the exact class scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py exists to prevent, in a guard whose own docstring says an unrecognised value 'must not arm anything'. [!] .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md BOTH still state this rule is CI-enforced by this script. That claim is now false, and a false claim of enforcement is worse than a stated absence: this repo's record is that the prose rule alone was read and disobeyed THREE TIMES, which is why the mechanism was built. [!] The lease is NOT to be resurrected -- the reset retired it deliberately. So the real question is what identifies the manager under the new operating model, where the manager's register is MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json and lanes are spawned as sessions with recorded ids. The `lane` field on a checklist row is a candidate identifier that did not exist when this guard was written.
